role: The code map's call graph: parses every Swift file with tree-sitter for calls, property reads, bare references, conformances and closure assignments; resolves each to unit keys as certain or possible edges; adds recorded calls, protocol-requirement dispatch and Makefile/workflow/script wiring. Imported by codemap.py (check, stamp, impact, callers) and report.py.
state: COMMON: member names (count, map, load, save, start, reset, ...) so common in Swift/Foundation/SwiftUI that a unique repo match on an unknown receiver is only a possible edge
NOT_A_REFERENCE: syntax-node parent types under which a simple_identifier is a declaration, label, type or member name rather than a reference
FUNC_KINDS / PROP_KINDS: inventory unit kinds that can be called / read as properties
toplevel: Module docstring defining certain and possible edges, `from __future__ import annotations`, imports (collections, re, Path, NS_CODE from inventory) and the three constants above. tree_sitter is imported inside build().

units.does: Parses one Swift file and walks it once, returning four things: refs (unit start line -> list of (kind 'call'|'prop', name, argument labels, trailing-closure count, (receiver kind, receiver type))), params (function/init/subscript start line -> [(external label, has default)]), conforms (type or protocol name -> names in its inheritance clause; extensions included, generic arguments and module prefixes stripped) and closure_assigns (stored-property name -> start lines of units that assign a closure literal to it). References in code outside every unit (Swift top-level code) are not collected.
Source text of a node: the raw bytes in its byte range, decoded with replacement.
For a call_expression, returns the label of each value argument in its call_suffix ('_' when unlabeled) and the number of trailing closures.

branches.cond: child is not the call suffix

units.does: Classifies what a member reference is made on: no target -> ('implicit', None); self or Self -> ('self', None); super -> ('super', None); a call whose callee is a capitalised identifier (a constructor, `Foo(...)`) -> ('type', 'Foo'); a capitalised dotted name -> ('type', its last component); anything else (a variable, a chain) -> ('unknown', None).

branches.cond: constructor call of a capitalised name

units.does: Recursive walk carrying the start line of the innermost enclosing unit. A class/struct/enum/extension/protocol declaration adds its inheritance clause to conforms. A function/init/deinit/subscript/protocol-function/property declaration that starts on a unit's start line becomes the current unit; for non-properties its parameters (external name, else name, else '_'; with whether a default follows) go to params. Inside a unit: a call on a bare identifier is an implicit-receiver call; a call on a navigation expression is a call with its receiver classified; a call on `.name` (implicit member) is a call with unknown receiver; prefix operators (`!f()`, `-f()`) are unwrapped to their operand first. A navigation expression that is not itself a callee is a property read with its receiver. A bare identifier not under a NOT_A_REFERENCE parent and not a callee is an implicit-receiver property read. An assignment whose right side is a closure literal records the target's last identifier in closure_assigns.

branches.effect: its inheritance specifiers added to conforms[name]

No parameter list known (None) matches anything.

units.does: Builds the whole graph. Nodes: every inventory unit (`path::key`) and every file (`path::`). Edges, each certain or possible (certain is never downgraded): (1) every `path::key` call named in a record (not ext:/dyn:/closure:) -> certain. (2) Swift: _swift_refs over every .swift file, conformances merged. A call on an implicit receiver whose name is a repo type is an initializer call: inits of that type whose labels match (certain if one). Calls/reads on self/super/implicit resolve within the unit's own type family (type, superclasses, protocols, transitively); an implicit one with no match falls back to same-file units, then to global functions. A receiver that is a repo type resolves within that type's family; a framework or unknown receiver resolves against every unit of that name and label set, and a single match on a COMMON name is only possible. An implicit property name with no match is ignored (a local). One candidate -> certain, several -> possible; a call with no candidate whose name is an assigned stored closure -> possible edges to the assigning units. (3) Each protocol requirement -> certain edge to each same-named, label-compatible function in a type conforming to that protocol. (4) Non-Swift code: a Makefile target -> its prerequisites; target recipes, workflow jobs and steps -> each `make`/`$(MAKE)` target and each scripts/ or Tools/ .sh/.py path (file node); a job -> its steps; Python and shell functions -> local functions (and, for Python, top-level defs imported from sibling modules via `from m import a` or `import m` + `m.a`) named in their body; file-level code outside units -> local functions and scripts it names. Returns {'edges': {src: {dst: kind}}, 'units': {node: inventory entry with file}}.

units.does: Units named `name` (Swift units and C/ObjC functions) that fit the reference: a call matches functions (whose labels bind, via _labels_match) and properties (a stored closure or computed value called); a property read matches properties and functions (a function reference). Optionally restricted to units with no enclosing type (global_only) or to units whose type is in `types`.
